newsitem.title: USA: Democrat chairman denies withholding documents.
newsitem.headline: Democrat chairman denies withholding documents.

text.p: Democratic Party chairman Roy Romer Friday denied intentionally withholding documents from a Senate committee investigating campaign fund raising scandals.

Romer, who is also governor of Colorado, told CNN there was nothing sinister in the sudden appearance of 4,000 new pages of documents from the files of former Democratic National Committee finance director Richard Sullivan.
"It is a mistake that should not have been made but it is an innocent one," Romer said.

The documents were handed over Monday, more than three months after the Senate Governmental Affairs Committee served the DNC with subpoenas for all relevant materials. They were discovered in a filing cabinet by Sullivan's successor, Paul DiNino. The committee is investigating the role of illegal foreign contributions in the 1996 elections.

Among the documents was a telephone call list of 12 prospective Democratic Party financial backers prepared for First Lady Hillary Rodham Clinton. A spokeswoman said Mrs. Clinton did not recall making any calls for contributions but she did not rule it out.

Romer said the DNC was going through 9 million documents to comply with the subpoenas. He said that if he found out that any DNC official was deliberately withholding documents from the committee, that official would be fired on the spot.
"We have absolutely no incentive to withhold anything," Romer said.

Sullivan was the first witness to testify when the committee began hearings last month. He said he had made an effort to find all his relevant documents and hand them over to the committee. However, he said he not taken detailed notes of his fund raising activities.

The committee's Republican chairman, Tennessee Sen. Fred Thompson, has accused the White House and the Democrats of doing all they could to delay his investigation, which is supposed to wrap up by December.
Committee sources said Thompson was determined to find out whether there was a Democratic coverup and had ordered investigators to interview DNC officials to find out who knew about the documents.
